title: OpenAI: Public Milestones Seed Timeline
description: A small official-source seed timeline. It is a starting point for reviewed expansion, not a comprehensive history.

events.title: OpenAI is introduced
events.summary: OpenAI published its introductory announcement and described itself as a nonprofit artificial intelligence research company.

sources.title: Introducing OpenAI
sources.claim_scope: OpenAI institutional introduction and nonprofit research-company description

events.interpretation: This is an appropriate public starting point for a timeline about OpenAI's institutional history.

events.title: OpenAI API launches in private beta
events.summary: OpenAI announced a private beta API for accessing new AI models through a general-purpose text-in, text-out interface.

sources.title: OpenAI API
sources.claim_scope: OpenAI API private-beta launch and general-purpose interface description

events.interpretation: This milestone marks an early public path from model research toward developer-facing infrastructure.

events.title: DALL-E is announced
events.summary: OpenAI announced DALL-E, a neural network trained to create images from text captions.
events.capability_implication: The public product surface expands from text generation into text-guided image creation.

sources.title: DALL-E: Creating images from text
sources.claim_scope: DALL-E announcement and text-guided image-generation description

events.interpretation: The announcement broadens the public timeline beyond language output into text-guided image generation.

events.title: OpenAI publishes the InstructGPT alignment method
events.summary: OpenAI published work on aligning language models to follow user intentions using reinforcement learning from human feedback.

sources.title: Aligning language models to follow instructions
sources.claim_scope: InstructGPT publication and reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedback method

events.interpretation: This records an alignment-method branch that later product milestones depend on but launch-only timelines often hide.
events.capability_implication: The work focuses on making model behavior better match user intent rather than increasing scale alone.
events.reliability_note: The publication discusses remaining limitations and should not be read as a claim that alignment is complete.
open_questions: How should timelines distinguish capability gains from improvements in instruction-following behavior?

events.title: ChatGPT launches publicly
events.summary: OpenAI opened ChatGPT to public feedback as a research preview.
events.social_implication: A public research preview made conversational AI directly accessible to a broad audience and created a new feedback surface.

sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT
sources.claim_scope: ChatGPT public research-preview launch

events.interpretation: The public launch of ChatGPT is a major product milestone and a useful anchor for later product changes.

events.title: OpenAI publishes its AGI planning statement
events.summary: OpenAI published a statement describing its approach to AGI development, deployment, alignment research, and public benefit.

sources.title: Planning for AGI and beyond
sources.claim_scope: OpenAI statement on AGI planning, deployment, alignment, and public benefit
sources.note: The official page states that its structural information was outdated as of October 28, 2025.

events.interpretation: This record preserves an attributable institutional voice about AGI planning. It is evidence of OpenAI’s stated position at the time, not proof that predictions or commitments will be realized.
events.social_implication: The statement frames AGI as a societal transition involving abundance, economic change, scientific discovery, and governance choices.
events.reliability_note: The source itself includes a later notice that some structural information became outdated.
open_questions: Which stated assumptions changed as OpenAI’s structure and deployment strategy evolved?

events.title: GPT-4 is announced
events.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-4 and described it as a large multimodal model accepting image and text inputs and emitting text outputs.
events.capability_implication: The announcement documents a shift from text-only interaction toward multimodal input.
events.reliability_note: The announcement describes capabilities, but a complete record should pair it with system-card evidence and known limitations.
open_questions: Which demonstrated capabilities were reliable enough for everyday use at launch?

sources.title: GPT-4
sources.claim_scope: GPT-4 announcement and multimodal-input description

events.interpretation: This milestone documents a major model-generation change after ChatGPT's public launch.

events.title: ChatGPT plugins enter alpha rollout
events.summary: OpenAI announced initial support for ChatGPT plugins and began extending alpha access to users and developers from a waitlist.
events.capability_implication: Plugins extend the product from conversation toward tool use and third-party actions.
events.reliability_note: The official page now notes that OpenAI plugins have been deprecated. The timeline should retain both introduction and later lifecycle context.

sources.title: ChatGPT plugins
sources.note: The official page now notes that OpenAI plugins have been deprecated.
sources.claim_scope: ChatGPT plugins alpha rollout and later deprecation note

events.interpretation: This milestone is useful for tracing how tool access and third-party integrations developed over time, including later deprecation.

events.title: DevDay introduces GPT-4 Turbo and Assistants API
events.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-4 Turbo, the Assistants API, and additional multimodal developer-platform capabilities at DevDay.
events.capability_implication: The developer platform adds more persistent, tool-oriented building blocks for assistant experiences.

sources.title: New models and developer products announced at DevDay
sources.claim_scope: GPT-4 Turbo, Assistants API, and DevDay developer-platform announcements

events.interpretation: This event captures a substantial expansion of the developer platform after the initial API beta.

events.title: GPT Store rollout begins
events.summary: OpenAI began rolling out the GPT Store to ChatGPT Plus, Team, and Enterprise users.

sources.title: Introducing the GPT Store
sources.claim_scope: GPT Store rollout and eligible ChatGPT plans

events.interpretation: This milestone documents a product-distribution layer for custom versions of ChatGPT.

events.title: OpenAI introduces the Model Spec
events.summary: OpenAI introduced a draft Model Spec describing intended model behavior and the objectives, rules, and default behaviors used to shape it.

sources.title: Introducing the Model Spec
sources.claim_scope: Draft Model Spec introduction and intended-behavior framework

events.interpretation: Behavioral guidance belongs beside model releases because it changes how systems are intended to act in public use.
events.social_implication: Publishing behavioral guidance creates a more inspectable interface between model development and public expectations.
open_questions: How should versioned behavior specifications be connected to deployment changes over time?

events.title: GPT-4o is introduced
events.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-4o as a new flagship model and described improvements across text, voice, and vision.
events.capability_implication: The product direction moves toward more fluid interaction across text, voice, and vision.
events.reliability_note: The announcement is an official capability claim. A fuller record should add system-card evidence and reviewed demonstrations.
open_questions: How consistently do multimodal improvements transfer into real-world workflows?

sources.title: Introducing GPT-4o and more tools to ChatGPT free users
sources.claim_scope: GPT-4o launch and text, voice, and vision improvements

events.interpretation: This is a later public product and model milestone that can be expanded with system-card evidence.

events.title: OpenAI publishes the GPT-4o System Card
events.summary: OpenAI published a system card covering the safety work, evaluations, and risk mitigations performed before releasing GPT-4o.

sources.title: GPT-4o System Card
sources.claim_scope: GPT-4o safety work, evaluations, and mitigations

events.interpretation: A separate system-card record makes evaluation history visible instead of burying it under the product launch.
events.reliability_note: System cards document evaluated risks and mitigations; they are not guarantees that every deployment risk is resolved.
open_questions: Which later product changes require updated evaluation records?

events.title: OpenAI o1-preview is released
events.summary: OpenAI released the first preview models in its o1 series in ChatGPT and the API, describing them as models designed to spend more time thinking before responding.
events.capability_implication: The public model line adds a reasoning-oriented branch designed to spend more time on a response.
events.reliability_note: The preview label matters: this record marks a public release, not a conclusion about general reliability.

sources.title: Introducing OpenAI o1-preview
sources.claim_scope: OpenAI o1-preview release and reasoning-model description

events.interpretation: This introduces a public reasoning-model branch in the product timeline.

events.title: Canvas enters beta
events.summary: OpenAI introduced canvas as an interface for collaborating with ChatGPT on writing and coding projects beyond a simple chat thread.

sources.title: Introducing canvas
sources.claim_scope: Canvas beta launch and interface description

events.interpretation: Canvas is a useful interface milestone: the product expands from conversational exchange into a shared workspace.
events.capability_implication: The interface supports iterative writing and coding collaboration in a separate working surface.

events.title: ChatGPT search is introduced
events.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT search with web answers that include links to relevant sources, initially for ChatGPT Plus and Team users and SearchGPT waitlist users.
events.capability_implication: The product adds a web-information layer with inspectable outbound source links.
events.reliability_note: Linked sources improve inspectability, but the presence of citations does not by itself verify every generated claim.
open_questions: How should readers evaluate source quality and claim-to-source alignment in generated answers?

sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT search
sources.claim_scope: ChatGPT search launch and outbound source-link behavior

events.interpretation: This event is directly relevant to a timeline project concerned with source trails and current web information.

events.title: Sora rolls out as a standalone product
events.summary: OpenAI moved its video-generation model out of research preview and began rolling out Sora Turbo at sora.com for ChatGPT Plus and Pro users.

sources.title: Sora is here
sources.claim_scope: Sora Turbo product rollout and lifecycle note
sources.note: The official page states that the Sora product is no longer available as of April 26, 2026.

events.interpretation: This records both a product launch and the importance of retaining lifecycle changes rather than treating launches as permanent states.
events.capability_implication: Video generation moves from research preview into a standalone product experience.
events.reliability_note: The official page records safety restrictions and a later product-status change.

events.title: Operator launches as a research preview
events.summary: OpenAI introduced Operator as a research preview of an agent that can use its own browser to perform tasks by typing, clicking, and scrolling.

sources.title: Introducing Operator
sources.claim_scope: Operator research-preview launch and browser-interaction description

sources.title: Operator System Card
sources.claim_scope: Operator safety evaluation and deployment mitigations

events.interpretation: This is a useful marker in the shift from conversational assistance toward agents acting through interfaces people already use.
events.capability_implication: Operator adds visual browser interaction through cursor and keyboard actions.
events.reliability_note: OpenAI labels Operator a research preview and documents mistakes, prompt injections, and harmful-task risks in the accompanying system card.
open_questions: Which classes of browser tasks remain reliable enough for routine delegated use?

events.title: Deep research is introduced
events.summary: OpenAI introduced deep research in ChatGPT as an agentic capability for multi-step research tasks that uses web browsing and Python tools.

sources.title: Introducing deep research
sources.claim_scope: Deep research launch and tool-use description

events.interpretation: This extends source-oriented search into longer-running research workflows.
events.capability_implication: The product can carry out multi-step web research with tool use rather than only returning a single search response.
events.reliability_note: Research output still requires source inspection and claim-level review.
open_questions: How consistently do generated reports align each material claim with the strongest available source?

events.title: OpenAI publishes an updated Model Spec
events.summary: OpenAI published an updated Model Spec with changes to its chain of command, customizability, transparency, and intellectual-freedom guidance.

sources.title: Sharing the latest Model Spec
sources.claim_scope: Updated Model Spec publication and highlighted behavior-guidance changes

events.interpretation: This adds a versioned governance layer: intended behavior changes over time and should be inspectable like product releases.
events.social_implication: Changes to default behavior and transparency guidance affect how users encounter the system in ordinary use.
open_questions: How should a timeline map Model Spec changes to specific deployed model behaviors?

events.title: GPT-4.5 enters research preview
events.summary: OpenAI released GPT-4.5 as a research preview and described it as its largest and best model for chat at the time.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-4.5
sources.claim_scope: GPT-4.5 research-preview release and stated product limitations

events.interpretation: The release documents a parallel capability path based on scaling pre-training rather than the reasoning-model branch alone.
events.capability_implication: OpenAI presents unsupervised learning and reasoning as complementary axes of model capability.
events.reliability_note: OpenAI described the release as a research preview and noted that GPT-4.5 did not support Voice Mode, video, or screensharing in ChatGPT at launch.

events.title: Responses API and Agents SDK launch
events.summary: OpenAI released the Responses API, built-in web search, file search and computer-use tools, the Agents SDK, and tracing tools for agentic applications.

sources.title: New tools for building agents
sources.claim_scope: Responses API, built-in tools, Agents SDK, and tracing launch

events.interpretation: This is a major developer-platform milestone for building inspectable agent workflows.
events.capability_implication: Developers gain a common API primitive with built-in tools, orchestration, guardrails, and execution tracing.
events.reliability_note: The announcement frames production reliability and visibility as active engineering concerns, not solved assumptions.
open_questions: How should agent traces be archived so later timelines can distinguish model capability from orchestration quality?

events.title: GPT-4.1 launches in the API
events.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and GPT-4.1 nano in the API, highlighting improvements in coding, instruction following, and long-context comprehension.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-4.1 in the API
sources.claim_scope: GPT-4.1 API-family launch and stated capability improvements

events.interpretation: This is a developer-platform milestone that adds a long-context model family and a smaller nano tier.
events.capability_implication: The announcement emphasizes coding, instruction following, and context windows up to one million tokens.

events.title: OpenAI releases o3 and o4-mini
events.summary: OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini as reasoning models with access to tools in ChatGPT and function calling in the API.

sources.title: Introducing OpenAI o3 and o4-mini
sources.claim_scope: o3 and o4-mini release, reasoning, and tool-use description

events.interpretation: This is a stronger bridge between reasoning models and agentic tool use.
events.capability_implication: The models can reason about when and how to use tools including web search, files, Python, visual inputs, and image generation.
events.reliability_note: OpenAI reports improved performance and accompanying safety evaluation; benchmark gains do not establish reliability across every workflow.
open_questions: Which tool-using workflows remain brittle despite improved benchmark performance?

events.title: Responses API adds MCP and more built-in tools
events.summary: OpenAI added remote MCP server support, image generation, Code Interpreter, file-search improvements, background mode, reasoning summaries, and encrypted reasoning items to the Responses API.

sources.title: New tools and features in the Responses API
sources.claim_scope: Responses API MCP support, tool expansion, and reliability features

events.interpretation: The agent platform becomes more interoperable and better suited to long-running work.
events.capability_implication: Agentic applications can connect remote MCP servers and use a broader set of built-in tools.
events.reliability_note: Background mode and observability-related features matter because longer workflows need recoverability and inspection.

events.title: ChatGPT agent is introduced
events.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT agent as a unified agentic system that can complete online tasks using its own virtual computer.

sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT agent: bridging research and action
sources.claim_scope: ChatGPT agent launch and unified agentic-system description

sources.title: ChatGPT agent System Card
sources.claim_scope: ChatGPT agent safety evaluation and safeguards

events.interpretation: This consolidates earlier browser-action and research branches into a broader product surface.
events.capability_implication: The system combines website interaction, research, and multi-step task completion through a virtual computer.
events.reliability_note: The system card documents safeguards and residual risks. A fuller record should continue tracking deployment changes over time.
open_questions: Which actions should remain confirmation-gated as agentic systems become more capable?

events.title: GPT-5 is introduced
events.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-5 as a unified system with a smart, efficient model, a deeper reasoning model, and a router that selects between them.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5
sources.claim_scope: GPT-5 launch and unified-system description

sources.title: GPT-5 System Card
sources.claim_scope: GPT-5 evaluation and safety documentation

events.interpretation: The product presentation moves toward a routed system rather than requiring users to choose every model branch manually.
events.capability_implication: OpenAI describes GPT-5 as combining efficient responses, deeper reasoning, and automatic routing.
events.reliability_note: The system card should remain the primary companion source for capability and safety claims.
open_questions: How should a public timeline represent routed systems when model behavior changes by task and deployment state?

events.title: GPT-5-Codex is released
events.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5-Codex as a version of GPT-5 optimized for agentic coding in Codex.

sources.title: Introducing upgrades to Codex
sources.claim_scope: GPT-5-Codex release and Codex product integration

sources.title: Addendum to GPT-5 system card: GPT-5-Codex
sources.claim_scope: GPT-5-Codex evaluation addendum

events.interpretation: This is a domain-specific agentic-coding milestone within the broader routed-system and agent-platform trajectory.
events.capability_implication: OpenAI describes GPT-5-Codex as supporting both interactive coding and longer independent software-engineering tasks.
events.reliability_note: The official release describes improved code review and longer task execution; the accompanying system-card addendum remains the appropriate evaluation companion.
open_questions: How should coding-agent timelines distinguish benchmark improvements from verified repository-level outcomes?

events.title: Sam Altman publishes OpenAI operating principles
events.summary: Sam Altman published a statement describing principles around broad access to AI, individual agency, safety, transparency, and the distribution of power.

sources.title: Our principles
sources.claim_scope: Sam Altman statement on OpenAI operating principles, access, agency, safety, and transparency

events.interpretation: This record captures an attributable executive statement about OpenAI’s current principles. It should be compared with observed decisions and later revisions rather than treated as an unquestionable account.
events.social_implication: The statement explicitly addresses who should hold power as AI capabilities increase and argues for broad access and individual agency.
open_questions: How will changes to operating principles be documented and compared with later deployment decisions?
